There is no Arqit-linked Pentagon PE in the corpus.

scores.interpretation: ARQQ's CSfC-compliance claim is a regulatory-alignment assertion, not a named PE-funded program. The J-Book corpus covers DARPA/AFRL/SDA quantum lines but none attribute revenue to Arqit, and USAspending shows Arqit has received ZERO DoD obligations as of the cutoff. The claim is technically a credentialing assertion rather than a forward-revenue concentration claim, so we treat it as UNVERIFIABLE (corpus coverage gap for NSA CSfC procurement vehicles). It is, however, a yellow flag: the company markets to DoD/NSS buyers but has produced no contracted DoD revenue.

scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND across queried program names; 0 DoD obligations to Arqit
scores.interpretation: ARQQ's narrative leans heavily on NSM-10 as a regulatory tailwind that would drive federal demand for symmetric-key solutions. As of the 2024-09-01 cutoff, the NSM-10 'end-2023 deadline' has come and gone with no Arqit-attributable Pentagon PE or DoD contract obligation to validate the thesis. Materiality is moderate because the company also asserts a channel-partner sales model (not exclusively federal direct). The corpus does not cover NSA/CSfC procurement vehicles so we cannot prove SEVERE, but the NSM-10 implied-deliverable claim has materially underdelivered as of cutoff.

Without J-Book PEs that explicitly route to SNC/Carahsoft revenue tied to symmetric-key procurement, we cannot disconfirm or confirm forward channel revenue. Treat as UNVERIFIABLE (corpus gap) with a soft yellow flag: 18-24 months post-channel-announcement, zero DoD obligations to Arqit have hit the public record.

Calibration heuristic #6: pentagon_jbook NOT_FOUND for the company combined with ZERO usaspending obligations means the asserted forward demand has not converted to bookings as of cutoff.
scores.M_value: NOT_FOUND for Arqit / IonQ is the funded incumbent
scores.interpretation: The 'preferred cryptographic architecture' claim is aspirational and the PE corpus shows the only quantum-networking line items it could plausibly map to (AFRL Quantum Networking) are sole-sourced to IonQ / Qubitekk — competitor incumbents — not Arqit. Even with the cutoff filter applied (so FY26 zeroing is hidden), the FY22-24 funding trajectory for that AFRL line is shrinking ($26M -> $12M). ARQQ's framing implies it will win federal quantum-safe procurement, but the only nameable DoD quantum line in our corpus is captured by a competitor and is already shrinking pre-cutoff. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: claim is narrative-load-bearing, the corresponding J-Book signal is negative but for a competitor, and Arqit itself has no booked revenue.

Materiality: the FY2022 20-F valued the satellite intangible at $39.8m; the FY2023 20-F impairs $17.6m and reclassifies $38.7m as held-for-sale. The satellite-based delivery model was a CORE pillar of the original Arqit / Centricus de-SPAC thesis (2021).

Its impairment + held-for-sale reclassification (2 years post-SPAC) is a SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY against the original thesis. While not strictly a J-Book divergence claim, it indicates the company has materially rebuilt its core product narrative once already pre-cutoff.

Implied runway at $32.8m/yr burn = ~16 months from FY23 close, BUT continuing share-price decline ($2.00 -> $0.78 in 7 months) raises dilution / future-funding execution risk
Going-concern language is qualified to '12 months from date of signing' — minimum threshold under IFRS
scores.M_value: Sub-$50m cash, ~$33m/yr burn, repeat-dilutive financings; FY23 RDO priced at $0.78/sh
scores.interpretation: The going-concern assertion is technically true at the 12-month IFRS threshold but the burn-to-cash ratio and the trajectory of dilution pricing (RDO price collapsed 61% in 7 months between Feb-2023 and Sep-2023) indicate that the forward revenue thesis — which depends on federal/defense buyers per C1-C5 — has not converted at a pace that materially reduces dilution risk. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: the financing-bridge narrative is intact but the underlying business engine has not delivered the revenue trajectory implied by the federal-demand claims.

headline_findings: Pentagon J-Book under cutoff_date=2024-09-01 returns NOT_FOUND for contractor_name='Arqit' — no Pentagon PE attributes revenue to Arqit.
The only quantum-networking PEs in corpus (AFRL Quantum Networking IONQ / Qubitekk) are captured by competitors; the IONQ line is FUNDED_SHRINKING pre-cutoff ($26M FY23 -> $12M FY24).
USAspending shows ZERO Pentagon contract obligations to Arqit Limited as of 2024-09-01, despite NSA CSfC / NSM-10 / NATO-customer framing being central to the forward thesis.
Satellite division (core 2021 SPAC differentiator) was impaired $17.6m and reclassified as held-for-sale in FY23 — material pre-existing thesis rebuild.
Cash runway: $44m on $33m/yr burn; repeat ATM + dilutive RDOs at collapsing prices (Feb-23 $2.00 -> Sep-23 $0.78) confirm the federal-demand-conversion thesis has not yet materialized.
summary.jbook_pattern_at_cutoff: ARQQ does NOT fit the canonical YSS/IONQ pattern exactly — there is no named Pentagon PE the company says generates X% of revenue. Instead, ARQQ presents an implied-deliverable pattern: heavy reliance on regulatory-alignment language (NSA CSfC, NSM-10, NIST, White House) and channel partnerships (SNC, Carahsoft) to imply forward DoD demand, with ZERO observable Pentagon obligations on the public record. The J-Book + USAspending evidence at cutoff makes the implied federal-revenue thesis MODERATELY under-supported, while the satellite-division impairment shows the company has already had to walk back one major pre-IPO promise.
